lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A shelf is 2.4 m long. Books are 3 cm thick. About how many books fit in a single row?

FEEDBACK
240 cm ÷ 3 cm = 80 books (estimate if spines vary).

WATCH FOR
Measuring twice with different units and comparing without converting leads to false fits.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve ten real-life measurement problems. Write a three-step plan (measure/unit/operate) for six.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Solve ten real-life measurement problems. Write a three-step plan (measure/unit/operate) for six. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for real-life; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Measuring twice with different units and comparing without converting leads to false fits.. Correction uses 240 cm ÷ 3 cm = 80 books (estimate if spines vary).. Why: restores accurate real-life.

Parent: Likely misconception: Measuring twice with different units and comparing without converting leads to false fits. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses real-life with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with real-life, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for real-life, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about real-life, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Will a 1.8 m desk fit a 160 cm gap? Convert 1.8 m = 180 cm > 160 cm → no. Check both readings.

TRY FIRST
A shelf is 2.4 m long. Books are 3 cm thick. About how many books fit in a single row?

FEEDBACK
240 cm ÷ 3 cm = 80 books (estimate if spines vary).
teach_steps.explain:
Real-life measurement problems need a plan: what to measure, which unit, whether to convert and how to check.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Measuring twice with different units and comparing without converting leads to false fits. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
